children: ended its relationship in Puerto Rico with local franchise operator Encanto Restaurants, which has led to the temporary closure of all KFC and Taco Bell locations in the nation. Both brands posted short statements saying Encanto had failed to meet their quality standards. The closures end long histories on the island. Puerto Rico’s first KFC opened in 1967, and Encanto began running Taco Bell there in 1985. Encanto has also operated Pizza Hut and IHOP restaurants in Puerto Rico.

The news comes at a hard time for the island’s restaurant industry. El Nuevo Día reported that one in three restaurants in Puerto Rico is considering closing. Looking ahead, KFC and Taco Bell said they are looking for a new franchise partner.

is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings before the opening bell on Tuesday. Analysts expect the fast-food chain operator to report revenue of $2.02B and earnings per share of $1.46. Shares of Yum! Brands
